claim: Let \(V=(\mathbb C^d,\|\cdot\|_V)\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(\mathcal E\) be any operator-space quantization of \(V\), and let \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)\in M_n(\mathbb C)^d\) be simultaneously triangularizable. In any common upper-triangular basis, write \(\lambda^{(k)}=((X_1)_{kk},\ldots,(X_d)_{kk})\in\mathbb C^d\) for \(1\le k\le n\). Then the Shalit--Shamovich spectral radius satisfies \[\rho_{\mathcal E}(X)=\max_{1\le k\le n}\|\lambda^{(k)}\|_V.\] Thus \(\rho_{\mathcal E}(X)\) is independent of the quantization on every simultaneously triangularizable matrix tuple, even when the matrices do not commute. In particular, the same formula holds whenever the complex Lie algebra generated by \(X_1,\ldots,X_d\) is solvable; consequently, if two quantizations of the same normed space give different spectral radii on a matrix tuple, the generated Lie algebra must be non-solvable.
scientific_limitations: Restricted to finite-dimensional complex matrix tuples that are simultaneously triangularizable, equivalently tuples generating a solvable complex Lie algebra.
The result concerns the Shalit--Shamovich spectral radius and does not assert the analogous formula for the minimal spectral radius.
Non-solvability is only a necessary condition for quantization dependence, not a sufficient condition for any prescribed pair of quantizations.
An older equivalent corollary under different spectral-radius terminology remains a residual literature risk because the proof is short and structural.
title: Quantization-independent spectral radius for simultaneously triangularizable matrix tuples
